_design_note: The budget question, reopened. Section 7.22 concluded budget is not a lever and section 7.26.2 found the opponent line flat from about round 2250 -- both measured at a CONSTANT step size. The L01 arm did not flatten: it climbed from 15.04 at round 2250 to 16.87 at 4750 and finished at 16.596. If that plateau was a step-size artefact rather than a ceiling, budget becomes a lever again under a decaying rate, and this arm is the test. L01 decays over 2500 ABSOLUTE rounds, so extending the budget does not stretch the schedule -- the confound E01 caused and section 7.22 had to unpick cannot recur here.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: training.budget.rounds 5000 -> 10000; the schedule is L01 in both, and being absolute it is bit-identical on rounds 1-5000
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: runs/m3_lr_decay_5000_vs3rb_20260827/ -- R02_9 with L01: repeat-measured tournament score 3.6371 (sd 0.121 over ten repeats), coins_share 0.3449, primary-suite 16.596
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: Within about 1.2 of the control on the primary suite means the plateau was a ceiling after all and section 7.22's conclusion stands as written, now with the step size controlled.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: None stated. L01 was never tuned; whether it is near the right shape is unknown.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: All five training-seed distributions, coins_share, the death split, the checkpoint curve (the control's did not flatten, unlike every constant-rate arm), and the ten repeat measurements individually.

_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: Ten repeats of classic_versus_opponents against the control's ten. A single measurement settles nothing (section 7.26.3).
